title: The Xylos Time Wobble
markdown:
On Xylos, time did a little jig. Not big dramatic leaps, but tiny boops and wiggles, as if a watch had taken a mini-nap or sped up for a second out of sheer excitement. In the middle of that slightly strange colony, the annual Interstellar Clockwork Competition was about to kick off. The air buzzed. Ozone mixed with freshly baked pastries, a Xylos specialty.

Iris, the Timekeeping Champion, could measure a nanosecond with her eyes closed. Everyone at the academy knew she could guess the exact moment a stubborn alarm clock would finally give up. Her hair gleamed like moonlight caught in a spiderweb, and it stayed perfectly styled even in zero gravity. Beside her, practically vibrating with suppressed silliness, was Dev the Prankster Genius. If there was a way to make a self-folding laundry bot do the cha-cha, or a holographic projector beam out embarrassing baby photos, Dev was already building it in his head, probably fueled by a questionable energy drink. He left a faint trail of sparks wherever he went.

“Are you sure about this, Dev?” Iris asked, her brow furrowed as she double-checked the perfectly aligned gears on her entry, a clock so elegant it looked like it belonged in a museum of perfect moments. Her voice was as smooth as polished brass. “The Chrono-Oscillator prototype… Mnemo says it’s experimental.” She gave the large pulsating device on the central pedestal a wary glance. It hummed with an almost musical, yet unsettling, energy.

Mnemo, the school’s super-smart, super-calm AI, hummed from the speakers in the competition hall’s ceiling. Mnemo was less a voice than a comforting, omnipresent presence. “Indeed, Iris,” Mnemo’s gentle electronic purr resonated. “The Chrono-Oscillator utilizes temporal resonance frequencies that have not been fully tested. My archives indicate a 3.7 percent chance of minor temporal anomalies. Potentially… wiggly.” Mnemo had a peculiar fondness for the word wiggly, a remnant of a long-forgotten debate with a philosophical hamster.

“Wiggly?” Dev snorted, a grin spreading so wide it threatened to split his cheeks. He nudged Iris. “Sounds like my kind of fun. Besides, Iris, your precision is legendary. We’ll be unbeatable. Plus, think of the bragging rights if we win with a slightly unpredictable device. Adds character, right?”

The competition began with a flourish of trumpets, actually synthesized by a particularly musical vacuum cleaner bot. Brilliant clocks, whirring gears, blinking lights: a symphony of timekeeping. Iris’s masterpiece ticked with perfect unwavering rhythm. Dev’s contraption, a clock that also made toast (always perfectly browned, unless Dev had tinkered with it too much) and told knock-knock jokes in a synthesized baritone, was a definite crowd favorite. Then it happened. The Chrono-Oscillator, a big glowing slightly unstable-looking sphere on a pedestal, began to pulse. Not a steady pulse. A nervous heartbeat. Thump-thump… THUMP-thump… THUMP-THUMP-THUMP-WOBBLE.

A competitor’s prize-winning timepiece, a magnificent golden owl that hooted the hours, started ticking backward, its hoots becoming annoyed squeaks. A perfectly timed announcement about the refreshment station’s famous stellar-berry tarts went silent mid-word, leaving everyone’s taste buds in bewildered anticipation. Iris glanced at her wrist. Her own perfect clock, the one she had set precisely, was spinning wildly, then just stopped. Frozen. “What in the…?” she gasped, her usual composure cracking. Dev’s toast-making clock, mid-ejection of a perfectly browned slice of artisanal rye, vanished. Poof.

“Whoa,” Dev yelled, ducking as a rogue perfectly spherical gear zipped past his ear with a high-pitched whizz. “My toast! That was artisanal rye, practically a national treasure.” He looked genuinely distraught, mischief briefly replaced by worry about his food.

Mnemo’s calm voice was a little flustered, which was very unlike the AI. “Temporal anomalies detected. Significant localized time slips. My sensors are fuzzy. It is like trying to read a book through a kaleidoscope while riding a unicycle.”

Iris, despite the rising panic and the distinct feeling that the floor beneath her feet was wobbling, felt a surge of determined focus. “Dev, we need to figure this out. Mnemo, what do you know about Xylos’s really old history? Not just the official academy records. Dig deeper. Legends. Whispers. Anything.”

Mnemo’s hum intensified, a sound like a thousand tiny gears whirring in unison. “Accessing deep archives. The legend of the Echoing Moments. A time on Xylos, eons ago, when the planet was said to be out of sync. They say moments could loop, or skip forward unexpectedly, or even mirror themselves. It is considered fanciful folklore by most historians.”

“Echoing Moments,” Iris murmured. She remembered a strange symbol etched on the Chrono-Oscillator’s base when they first saw it. It looked vaguely familiar, like something she had glimpsed in the dusty corners of the academy’s oldest wing. “Dev, that symbol. It is like the one on that old inscription near the archive sector. The one they said was from a forgotten inventor.”

Dev’s eyes lit up, mischief returning with a scientific curiosity. He was already halfway to the inscription, leaving a faint trail of tiny sparking wires. “Forgotten inventor, you say? Sounds like someone who knew how to make things interesting. And possibly a little temporally untidy.”

They found the inscription tucked away in a rarely visited alcove. It was faded, almost swallowed by time itself, but Mnemo projected a clearer brighter image onto a nearby wall. It spoke of tuning the heart of time and listening to the whispers of yesterday and tomorrow. And there, scribbled in a corner like an afterthought, was a series of odd, almost musical notes.

“Musical notes?” Iris frowned, tapping her chin. “How does that help us with time? Unless the inventor was also a composer of temporal lullabies.”

“Wait, wait, wait,” Dev yelped, already pulling a small whirring device from his pocket. It looked like a tiny music box that had had a passionate affair with a very confused spider, with more dials and antennae than seemed strictly necessary. “I built this ages ago. It is a sonic synchronizer. It translates certain frequency patterns into… well, into something. I was testing it on my alarm clock, but it never quite worked. It got stuck on a loop that sounded like this.” He fiddled with a dial, and a strange warbling melody filled the air.

Wibble-wobble, hum-de-dum, echo-pop.

Mnemo chimed in, its voice regaining some of its usual clarity. “Analyzing sonic pattern. This pattern is the inverse resonance frequency of the Chrono-Oscillator’s primary temporal stabilizer. A counter-tune. A temporal antidote, if you will.”

“You mean,” Iris breathed, her mind racing faster than a runaway clock, “that old inventor did not just write a legend. They left us a fix. A way to balance it out.”

The Chrono-Oscillator was pulsing erratically now. The whole hall shimmered with an iridescent light. Objects flickered in and out of existence like shy ghosts. The competition sat on the verge of total temporal collapse, a disaster zone of scrambled seconds and misplaced minutes. Dev scrambled toward the Chrono-Oscillator, sonic synchronizer clutched in his hand.

“Iris, you need to fine-tune the energy flow,” Mnemo instructed, a steady guide amidst the chaos. “The echoes of past moments are fighting the core mechanism. You have to be precise, but also flexible.”

Iris, her hands steady despite the temporal wobbles that threatened to send her spinning, began adjusting the delicate dials on the Chrono-Oscillator. It was like conducting an orchestra made of lightning. Dev cranked up the sonic synchronizer, its strange warbling tune filling the space, a defiant melody against the temporal clash. Wibble-wobble, hum-de-dum, echo-pop. The flickering lights began to steady, as if being drawn back into place. The random backward ticks of other clocks slowed, then stopped. The shimmer faded, replaced by the familiar solid walls of the competition hall. The Chrono-Oscillator pulsed one last time, a steady harmonious glow, and then silence. A profound, blessed silence.

A collective sigh of relief. Everyone looked around, a little dazed but incredibly grateful. Their watches were still a little off. Some were ten minutes fast, some ten minutes slow, some stubbornly insisting it was Tuesday when it was clearly Friday. Dev’s toast-making clock reappeared with a soft pop, looking slightly confused and holding a single perfectly browned slice of artisanal rye. The temporal meltdown was over.

The judges, thoroughly bewildered but a little impressed by the sheer spectacle, awarded Iris and Dev a special commendation. “For exceptional temporal problem-solving,” one judge stammered, still trying to reset his own wristwatch, which was now displaying a picture of a small fluffy alien.

Iris smiled, a genuine happy smile that reached her eyes. Precision had not been enough on its own. She had had to listen, and then let Dev’s messy little song do the rest.

Dev, holding his reappeared toast protectively, winked. “And sometimes,” he added, taking a delighted bite, “a little temporal wobble makes for a much more interesting competition. More spice.” He made a dramatic gesture with the toast.

Mnemo hummed contentedly. “Indeed. My archives now include a new entry: Temporal Wobbles. Manageable with witty ingenuity, a silly song, and a delicious piece of toast.”

On the colony of Xylos, where time liked to play peek-a-boo, the clocks never quite agreed again. Iris watched Dev finish the rye. The hall smelled of ozone and pastry. Somewhere, a golden owl hooted the correct hour, then thought better of it, and went quiet.
characters: Iris (timekeeping champion), Dev (prankster genius), Mnemo (school archive AI)
